title: Nonabelian level structures on elliptic curves
summary: Plan elliptic curves equipped with connected finite nonabelian torsors, their admissible compactification and cuspidal automorphisms. The cotangent line along the ramification divisor yields a divisibility theorem for coarse component degrees. Finite group estimates and rank-two SL2 trace coordinates translate it into Nielsen orbit congruences, leading to conditional connectedness, genus, finiteness and noncongruence results for Markoff modular curves.
readme: This roadmap specializes the general Hurwitz and stack foundations to one-pointed genus-one targets. It imports stable-curve gluing, tangential Galois theory, classical modular curves, integral invariants and Markoff moves from their owners. Its eight layers follow the proof dependencies, from the sheaf of G-structures and cusp data to cotangent degree and SL2 orbit congruences. The current published Chen paper is the primary source; all results are stated in our own words, with printed page and theorem numbers in the packet and reader. The complete planning pass leaves explicit supplier requests and four gaps; it makes no implementation or closure claim. The general-j finite-group claim is restricted to j=0, and genus applications consume the independently owned finite-field dynamics inputs after NL.6.

stages.title: Elliptic nonabelian level structures
stages.description:
**The elliptic admissible-cover specialization.** For finite G and S over Z[1/|G|], restrict the imported admissible (g,n)-cover stack to (1,1), identifying a stable one-pointed genus-one target with a 1-generalized elliptic curve E/S. Write A_G for this stack and A_G^0 for its smooth-target open. Retain the imported finite quotient map C→E, connected prestable source, G-torsor off the origin and nodes, tame cyclic inertia, and balanced charts x=ξ^e at a marking and (x,y)=(ξ^r,η^r), ξη=a, xy=a^r at a node. The quotient map is finite; flatness is not imposed at a ramified node. The full marking is the reduced ramified fibre for e>1 and the full étale fibre for e=1.

**The reduced ramification divisor.** For an elliptic admissible cover π:C→E over S, let Δ(H) be the smooth fixed locus C_sm^H with all fixed loci C_sm^K for strictly larger cyclic K removed. Define R_π as the disjoint union of Δ(H) over nontrivial cyclic H≤G, with the induced fixed-locus scheme structures. It is an effective Cartier divisor finite étale over S, with geometrically reduced fibres; it is reduced as a scheme if S is reduced. The converse holds when R_π→S is surjective, in particular for e≥2 on a nonempty connected base. On a connected base the origin ramification index e is constant; if e≥2, R_π has degree |G|/e and is the fibrewise reduced origin fibre. If e=1, R_π is empty and the full marking is the whole étale origin fibre.

**Monodromy of the ramification divisor.** Assume S connected and π as above with e≥2. For a geometric ramified point x with inertia H, all connected components of R_π are isomorphic finite étale Galois covers of S. Their deck groups embed in N_G(H)/H. If S is regular integral and contains a primitive e-th root of unity, these groups embed in C_G(H)/H. For a connected component X of A_G over Z[1/|G|,ζ_e], the same assertion holds for the universal ramification divisor, by finite étale monodromy and descent of the inertia character.

**The Higman invariant.** Fix ζ_n on a Z[1/|G|]-base, with every inertia order e dividing n. At a point x over O the faithful action on its cotangent line is χ_x:H→μ_e. Define Hig_ζ(π) in ConjClasses(G) as the class of the unique c in H with χ_x(c)=ζ_n^(n/e). Set e=1 and c=1 in the unramified case. This is independent of the point and compatible with base change and isomorphisms. With right G-actions and a positively oriented punctured-torus basis (a,b), the positive peripheral loop is [b,a], for [x,y]=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}.

**Open and closed Higman strata.** The index e and Hig_ζ are locally constant on A_G and on its smooth locus. Hence, after adjoining the requisite roots, each fixed conjugacy class gives an open and closed substack, and the disjoint union of these substacks is the whole moduli stack. The decomposition descends through the central rigidification and agrees on coarse spaces.

**The sheaf of G-structures.** On the étale site of the elliptic moduli stack over Z[1/|G|], T_G is the sheafification of the presheaf assigning to E/S the isomorphism classes of right G-torsors over E\O with geometrically connected fibres over S. A G-structure is a section of this sheaf; M(G) is its associated stack over M(1). Over a separably closed field these sections are actual torsor classes. For center-free G the presheaf is already a sheaf. For general bases and nontrivial center, sheaf sections are not identified with global torsors without descent data.

**Geometry of the finite étale level stack.** M(G)→M(1) is representable finite étale over Z[1/|G|]. M(G) is smooth separated Deligne–Mumford. Its coarse scheme is normal affine, finite over the affine j-line, smooth of relative dimension one over Z[1/|G|], and étale away from j=0,1728. Formation of this coarse scheme commutes with a base change to a regular Noetherian base, or to an arbitrary base when 6 divides |G|. A non-two-generated G gives the empty stack.

**Elliptic monodromy and branch cycles.** Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, use a complex comparison and a positively oriented basis of F2=π1(E\O) to identify the geometric fibre of M(G) with Epi^ext(F2,G). The connected components are Out^+(F2)-orbits. On exterior pairs the branch operators are γ0(a,b)=(ab^{-1},a), γ1728(a,b)=(b^{-1},a), γ∞(a,b)=(a,ab), and γ−I(a,b)=(a^{-1},b^{-1}). The generic coarse fibre is the quotient by γ−I, and fibres at 0,1728,∞ are respectively quotients by γ0, γ1728, and the subgroup generated by γ−I and γ∞. Stack monodromy uses π1(M(1)^an), not π1 of the coarse affine line.

**Elliptic boundary deformation and density.** At a geometric object in characteristic prime to |G|, the elliptic admissible-cover deformation map on universal rings is Λ[[T]]→Λ[[t]], T↦t^r, for a Cohen ring Λ and node stabilizer order r; for a smooth object r=1. Consequently A_G→Mbar(1) is flat proper quasi-finite and its smooth-target open is dense. In particular the entire compactification is empty if G is not two-generated.

**Central rigidification and compactification.** Define Mbar(G)=A_G rigidified by Z(G), using the imported central subgroup of the vertical inertia. Its open M(G) is identified with A_G^0 rigidified by Z(G). The rigidification has the same coarse scheme as A_G. Both compactified stacks are smooth proper relative curves over Z[1/|G|]; Mbar(G)→Mbar(1) is flat proper quasi-finite, and the coarse scheme is smooth proper of relative dimension one. Representability at the boundary requires a separate vertical-automorphism computation and is not automatic.

**Functoriality under quotients of G.** For a surjection f:G1→G2 of finite two-generated groups, f induces M(G1)→M(G2) by quotienting a connected torsor by ker f, and a proper surjective quasi-finite extension Mbar(G1)→Mbar(G2). On geometric fibres this is postcomposition on exterior epimorphisms and is compatible with Higman classes. Surjectivity of the stack morphism uses lifting of generating pairs up to monodromy, equivalently the group-theoretic lifting theorem used in Chen; it is not inferred merely from surjectivity of G1→G2 on elements.

**Absolute and intermediate level structures.** For A≤Out(G), define T_{G|A}=T_G/A and M(G|A)=M(G)/A, with M(G)^abs for A=Out(G). The Out(G)-action on the geometric fibre T_G is free, hence the quotient is another finite locally constant sheaf; the same quotient notation on smooth compactifications means normalization of the coarse quotient, or the corresponding stack quotient with its residual stabilizers retained. A fixed Higman stratum is used only when A preserves that class, or else replaced by its A-orbit.

**Cofinality of elliptic nonabelian levels.** Every connected finite étale cover of M(1) over Qbar is dominated by a connected component of M(G) for some finite two-generated G. Consequently, for any smooth projective geometrically connected curve X/Qbar there is a nonempty open U⊂X and a component N of an elliptic nonabelian level curve with a finite étale Galois map N→U. The target is the open curve U, not the whole projective X.

stages.title: Cusps and their finite data
stages.description:
**Normalization and gluing data at a cusp.** Fix an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k, compatible primitive roots, a nodal elliptic curve E and a standard normalization ν:P¹→E taking 1 to O and identifying 0 with ∞. A gluing datum is a finite right G-equivariant map q:D→P¹ from a possibly disconnected smooth curve whose restriction over P*=P¹\{0,1,∞} is a right G-torsor, together with a G-equivariant bijection α between the reduced fibres D_0 and D_∞. Morphisms are G-equivariant cover isomorphisms respecting α. A precuspidal cover of E means the finite quotient obtained by gluing, without imposing flatness at its nodes.

**The cusp normalization equivalence.** The normalization functor is an equivalence between precuspidal covers of E and gluing data relative to ν. Its inverse is the scheme pushout identifying each x∈D_0 with α(x)∈D_∞. The pushout is prestable, has normalization D, is unchanged off the glued fibres, and its local functions are precisely those with equal values on each paired pair. Connected balanced objects correspond exactly to the cusp fibre A_G×_{Mbar(1)}{E}; automorphisms over E are vertical automorphisms.

**Finite precuspidal data.** For a good tangential path δ: t0→t∞ on P*=P¹\{0,1,∞}, let Π=π1(P*,t0), a free profinite group generated by γ0 and γ∞^δ=δ^{-1}γ∞δ. A precuspidal G-datum is a finite set F with a continuous left Π-action and a commuting free transitive right G-action, and a G-equivariant bijection α:⟨γ0⟩\F→⟨γ∞^δ⟩\F. For x∈F, define ϕ_x by γx=xϕ_x(γ) and H_{δ,x}={h:α([x]_0)=[x]_∞h}. This is the left coset ⟨ϕ_x(γ∞^δ)⟩h, not a chosen element.

**The graph of a glued cover.** The graph of (F,α) uses the imported nodal-curve half-edge graph: vertices are Π\F, half-edges are ⟨γ0⟩\F disjoint union ⟨γ∞^δ⟩\F, incidence is projection to Π-orbits, and the fixed-point-free reversal pairs the two summands via α and α^{-1}. It identifies with the geometric dual graph of the glued cover and admits loops and multiple edges. It is connected iff ⟨ϕ_x(Π),h⟩=G for one, equivalently every, x and h∈H_{δ,x}.

**Balance and connectedness in finite data.** The glued cover is balanced iff ϕ_x(γ0)^{-1}=h^{-1}ϕ_x(γ∞^δ)h for one, equivalently every, x and h∈H_{δ,x}. Together with graph connectedness, this is equivalent to the two conditions ϕ_x(γ0)=h^{-1}u^{-1}h and ⟨u,h⟩=G, where u=ϕ_x(γ∞^δ). The normalization, fibre and gluing equivalences restrict to connected, balanced and cuspidal full subgroupoids.

**The cusp invariant set I(G).** Let Gen2(G)={(u,h):⟨u,h⟩=G}. Define I(G) as Gen2(G) modulo simultaneous conjugation by G and the commuting Z-action (u,h)↦(u,u^k h). Write [[u,h]] for the class. The second move is left multiplication of h by an integer power of u. This quotient classifies cusp isomorphism classes only after a good path and a standard normalization have been selected.

**Standard cusp from a generating pair.** For a generating pair (u,h), take F=G as a right torsor, let γ∞^δ act by left multiplication by u and γ0 by left multiplication by h^{-1}u^{-1}h, and define α(⟨h^{-1}u^{-1}h⟩x)=⟨u⟩hx. This is a connected balanced datum. Its normalization monodromy is M_{u,h}=⟨u,h^{-1}u^{-1}h⟩; its glued curve has [G:M_{u,h}] irreducible components.

**Classification of cusps and their Higman class.** The assignment (F,α)↦[[ϕ_x(γ∞^δ),h]] is independent of x and h and gives a bijection from isomorphism classes in the fixed cusp fibre of A_G to I(G), with inverse the standard construction. For [[u,h]], the Higman class is the class of [u^{-1},h^{-1}], which is conjugate to [u,h]. This is a bijection on isomorphism classes; it does not discard the automorphism groups of the cusp stack.

**Inversion of the target at a cusp.** Choose a symmetric good path. Pullback by [−1] on the nodal elliptic target sends [[u,h]] to [[u^{-1},h^{-1}]]. The target involution lifts to the cover iff these classes agree, equivalently iff (u^{-1},h^{-1}) is simultaneously conjugate to (u,u^r h) for some integer r. Existence of a lift does not choose a splitting of the resulting automorphism-group extension.

stages.title: Cusp automorphism groups
stages.description:
**The cusp automorphism group A(G,u,h).** For finite G and generating (u,h), put M=⟨u,h^{-1}u^{-1}h⟩ and A(G,u,h)={a∈C_G(M):[a,h]∈⟨u⟩}. Let k_{u,h} be the least positive k such that (u,h) is simultaneously conjugate to (u,u^k h); it exists since k=|u| works. Retain Mathlib centralizers, cyclic subgroups and element orders. The restriction z(a)=[a,h] takes values in ⟨u⟩.

**The cusp automorphism exact sequence.** For the preceding data, ker z=Z(G), im z=⟨u^{k_{u,h}}⟩ and 1→Z(G)→A(G,u,h)→⟨u^{k_{u,h}}⟩→1 is exact. In particular |A|=|Z(G)|·|u|/k_{u,h}. Evaluation at 1 identifies A with automorphisms of the standard datum, hence with vertical automorphisms of its glued cover.

**Full and marked cusp stabilizers.** For a cusp [[u,h]], Aut^v=A(G,u,h). The full automorphism group equals A if [[u,h]] is not fixed by inversion, and otherwise is an extension 1→A→Aut→C2→1. At a ramification point above O the vertical stabilizer is A∩⟨[u^{-1},h^{-1}]⟩. The cover is irreducible iff M_{u,h}=G. Moreover Mbar(G)→Mbar(1) is representable iff A(G,u,h)=Z(G), equivalently k_{u,h}=|u|, for every generating pair.

**Comparison with abelian full levels.** For abelian G, every cusp has A(G,u,h)=G=Z(G), so the rigidified forgetful map is representable. For G=(Z/n)^2 with n≥3, the resulting compactified full-level stack agrees with the existing Deligne–Rapoport full-level problem over Z[1/n], respecting determinant/Weil-pairing components; its cuspidal objects have no residual automorphisms. This is a comparison with the imported full-level carrier, not a second construction of modular curves.

**The odd-dihedral obstruction example.** For G=D_{2k}, k odd and k≥3, a generating pair has commutator of order k, but each compactified coarse component has degree 3 over P¹_j; there are φ(k)/2 components. The centralizer obstruction is d′=1, while m′=k; for a rotation u and a reflection h, M=⟨u⟩, A=⟨u⟩ and k_{u,h}=1. Thus divisibility of the coarse degree by the inertia order can fail arbitrarily strongly.

stages.title: Cotangent lines and degree congruences
stages.description:
**The universal section cotangent line.** On A_G with origin inertia e≥2, let R be the universal reduced ramification divisor. For a connected component R_X over a component X of A_G, pull back the universal source C and target E to R_X and use its tautological section σ of C. The line L=σ*ω_{C/R_X} is canonically the conormal of σ and has a base-change-compatible isomorphism L^⊗e ≅ f*λ, where λ=O*ω_{E/A_G}. Here f:R_X→X→Ell_1 and ω is the relative dualizing line on the imported prestable family. The section is contained in C_sm, even at a cuspidal moduli point.

**The stack Hodge degree.** Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, deg_{Ell_1}(λ)=1/24. For a proper smooth connected tame Deligne–Mumford curve Y with generic stabilizer order n_Y and a line whose stabilizer characters all vanish, its degree lies in (1/n_Y)Z. If g:Y→X is nonconstant between such curves, then deg_Y(g*L)=(n_X/n_Y) deg(g_coarse) deg_X(L). Degrees here are the rational stack degrees imported from SF.5, not degrees on coarse curves without the stabilizer correction.

**The cotangent and cover obstructions.** For a connected characteristic-zero component X⊂A_G of inertia e≥2, define d_X as the degree of the induced map of coarse curves R_X^coarse→X^coarse for a connected component of universal R. Define m_X as the least positive integer killing the stabilizer character of L at every geometric point of R_X. Define m′_X similarly using only vertical automorphisms over the target elliptic curve. All components R_X are isomorphic, and these integers are independent of their choice. Finite inertia and finite type make the least common multiples finite; use exponent 1 for trivial characters.

**Full and vertical character bounds.** With the preceding hypotheses, m′_X divides m_X and m_X divides 12m′_X. Also d_X divides |C_G(⟨c⟩)/⟨c⟩| for the Higman generator c. At a smooth cover Aut^v(C,π,x)=Z(G)∩⟨c⟩. At an arbitrary ramification point its vertical automorphism group acts faithfully on the cotangent line: use freeness on the punctured smooth branch, together with the finite-order tame local action, rather than a general assertion that tangent representations are faithful.

**The component degree congruence.** Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic zero, G finite, X a connected component of A_G,k of inertia e≥2, and d_X,m_X as above. Then 12e/gcd(12e,m_X d_X) divides deg(X^coarse→P¹_j). In particular the degree is positive and the assertion concerns the whole compactified coarse component; its smooth open has the same generic degree.

**The finite group obstruction pair.** For finite G and c∈G, let P_c be the generating pairs (u,h) for which [u,h] is conjugate to c. For each pair put M=⟨u,h^{-1}u^{-1}h⟩ and A={a∈C_G(M):[a,h]∈⟨u⟩}, as in NL.2. Define m′_c to be the least common multiple, over P_c, of the exponents of A∩⟨[u^{-1},h^{-1}]⟩. Define d′_c=|C_G(⟨c⟩)/⟨c⟩|. Each intersection is cyclic; the least common multiple of an empty family is 1. These are invariants of the conjugacy class of c.

**The Higman and Nielsen congruences.** For any nonempty characteristic-zero G-cover component with Higman class c, the integer |c|/gcd(|c|,m′_c d′_c) divides its coarse j-degree. It also divides the cardinality of every Out^+(F2)-orbit on Epi^ext(F2,G) of that class. The unquotiented orbit has the coarse degree or twice that degree, according as γ−I fixes or does not fix an exterior pair. The claim is not that this modulus divides the number of cusps.

stages.title: Finite group obstruction bounds
stages.description:
**The normal-subgroup-free obstruction bound.** Let ℓ be prime, G finite nonabelian and c∈G, with r=ν_ℓ(|c|) and r+s=ν_ℓ(|G|). Assume G has no proper normal subgroup whose order is divisible by ℓ. If k=ν_ℓ(m′_c)>0, then G contains C_{ℓ^k}×C_{ℓ^k}, hence 2k≤r+s. Also ν_ℓ(d′_c)≤s. Consequently ν_ℓ(m′_c)≤⌊(r+s)/2⌋. This is the j=0 case only; it does not assert the printed general-j bound.

**The prime-power component bound.** Under the hypotheses of the preceding bound, every nonempty Higman-c component and every associated Out^+(F2)-orbit has degree or size divisible by ℓ^max(⌈(r−3s)/2⌉,0). Here r=ν_ℓ(|c|) and r+s=ν_ℓ(|G|); ℓ need not be odd. This output uses only the proved j=0 obstruction estimate.

**The simple-group congruence.** Let G be finite nonabelian simple and not isomorphic to PSL2(F_q) for any prime power q. Let c∈G have ℓ-primary order ℓ^r with ℓ prime and ℓ^(r+1)≥|G|^(1/3). Assuming the abelian-subgroup cube bound |B|³<|G| for every abelian B≤G, every associated component degree and Out^+(F2)-orbit size is divisible by ℓ^⌈r/2⌉. The named unconditional theorem needs the missing Vdovin input G-VDOVIN; the conditional deduction is completely specified here.

stages.title: Rank-two trace coordinates
stages.description:
**Trace strata of SL2-covers.** For a prime power q and an SL2(F_q)-cover over Qbar, fix the compatible roots exp(2πi/n) through a chosen embedding in C. Define its trace invariant t as tr(c), where c is its Higman representative in SL2(F_q). Conjugacy invariance makes it independent of the ramification point. The t-strata are unions of Higman strata and are open and closed. The invariant descends through central rigidification and GL2(F_q)-conjugation. The root convention is part of the definition; arbitrary coprime powers of c need not preserve its trace.

**Admissible trace classes.** Call a conjugacy class, or trace, q-admissible if it occurs as the commutator class, or trace, of a generating pair of SL2(F_q). For G=SL2(F_q), a trace t occurs as the commutator of a generating pair precisely as follows: all t≠2 for q=2,4,8 or q≥13; all t other than 1,2 for q=3,9,11; all t other than 0,2,4 for q=5; all t other than 0,1,2 for q=7. For t≠±2 there is one SL2-conjugacy class of trace t. When q is odd and −2 is admissible there are two admissible noncentral classes of trace −2, interchanged by a nonsquare-determinant GL2-conjugation. The central class of −I is excluded from these two classes.

**The noncentral trace order.** For a∈F_q define n_q(a) to be the order of any noncentral element of SL2(F_q) of trace a. For q even and a=0 it is 2. For q odd, n_q(2)=p and n_q(−2)=2p. In every other case, choose a root ω of X²−aX+1 in F_{q²}; then n_q(a)=ord(ω), independent of the root. This definition excludes central matrices, whose orders at traces ±2 would be different.

**The rank-two SL2 character scheme.** For every commutative ring R, take the existing affine scheme SL2_R×SL2_R with diagonal GL2_R-conjugation. Its affine invariant quotient is the rank-two SL2 character scheme. The map (A,B)↦(tr A,tr B,tr AB) induces an isomorphism of invariant coordinate algebras R[x,y,z]≅O(SL2²)^GL2, and hence an isomorphism of the quotient with A³_R, compatible with every ring base change. Invariants here mean the group-scheme coaction, not invariance under only the finite group of R-valued points.

**The commutator trace polynomial.** For any commutative ring R and A,B∈SL2(R), with x=tr A,y=tr B,z=tr AB, one has tr([A,B])=x²+y²+z²−xyz−2. Thus the fixed commutator-trace fibre t is the already-owned CA.4 Markoff level surface of level t+2. The identity is integral, including residue characteristics 2 and 3.

**Outer automorphisms in trace coordinates.** Right precomposition by Aut(F2) induces an antihomomorphism to polynomial automorphisms of A³_R. It factors through Out(F2)/⟨−I⟩≅PGL2(Z). The Nielsen generators r:(a,b)↦(a^{-1},b), s:(a,b)↦(b,a), t:(a,b)↦(a^{-1},ab) act by (x,y,xy−z), (y,x,z), (x,z,y). The central −I acts trivially. This identifies the image with the group generated by these Vieta/permutation moves, but asserts no faithfulness. The full CA.4 Markoff group also has even sign changes and must be compared as a larger group.

**The matrix-algebra criterion.** For a commutative ring R and A,B∈SL2(R), the R-subalgebra generated by A and B is M2(R) iff tr([A,B])−2=x²+y²+z²−xyz−4 is a unit. Over a field this is equivalent to absolute irreducibility of the associated two-generator representation, using the existing R01.1 predicate. Over a general ring the conclusion is the full matrix-algebra condition; no field-only representation predicate is silently extended.

**Finite-field trace fibres.** For every finite field F_q the trace map SL2(F_q)²→F_q³ is surjective. On the absolutely irreducible locus it induces a bijection from simultaneous GL2(F_q)-conjugacy classes to triples with x²+y²+z²−xyz−2≠2. No surjectivity from generating pairs is asserted for all triples. In particular the GL2 quotient must be distinguished from the finer SL2 quotient in odd characteristic.

**The diagonal outer group.** For G≤SL2(F_q), define D(q,G) to be the image of N_GL2(F_q)(G) in Out(G), equivalently N_GL2(F_q)(G)/(G·C_GL2(F_q)(G)). For G=SL2(F_q), write D(q); its order is 1 for even q and 2 for odd q, and for prime p, D(p)=Out(SL2(F_p)). This is the group which identifies SL2-conjugacy classes within one GL2-conjugacy class.

**Rationality of SLn normalizers.** Let q be a prime power and n≥2. The normalizer of SL_n(F_q) in GL_n(F̄_q) is F̄_q^×·GL_n(F_q). For n=1 both sides equal F̄_q^×. Consequently an algebraic-closure conjugator between the standard full SL_n(F_q) groups can be rescaled to an F_q-rational conjugator. This is the specific normalizer theorem used here, not a new general Skolem–Noether development. The same normalizer formula holds with GL_n(F_q) in place of SL_n(F_q).

**The non-dihedral subgroup refinements.** For q≥3 and an absolutely irreducible non-dihedral G≤SL2(F_q), the projective image is a subfield PSL2 or PGL2 group, or A4,S4,A5, with the characteristic-dependent cases and subfield embeddings supplied by Dickson classification. Then |D(q,G)|≤2. Every such G contains Z(SL2(F_q)). Its cusp-automorphism consequence is proved in NL.6 using the rotation period, rather than assumed from classification. The printed S5 is replaced by S4, and the quotient in the outer bound is N/(G·C).

stages.title: SL2 stabilizers and orbit congruences
stages.description:
**The geometric trace subsets.** Use the imported CA.4 surface at level t+2 for X_t(q). Define X_t*(q) as its triples corresponding under the finite-field trace bijection to absolutely irreducible representations whose projective image is neither trivial nor dihedral; the dihedral group of order 2 is included in the exclusion. Define X_t°(q) by surjectivity onto SL2(F_q). For t≠2, X_t*(q) consists exactly of triples having at least two nonzero coordinates. Both subsets at t=2 are empty. For q≥3, X_t°⊂X_t*; for q=2, X*(2) is empty and X°(2) is not. For prime p≥3 and t=−2, both subsets equal the punctured Markoff surface. This last equality is not extended to proper prime-power fields.

**The trace and moduli correspondence.** Let q≥3, let ϕ:F2→SL2(F_q) have absolutely irreducible non-dihedral image G, and let P be its trace triple. The fibre of M(G)/D(q,G) over a geometric elliptic curve is Epi^ext(F2,G)/D(q,G); trace identifies it with the triples having GL2-conjugate image G. Its Out^+(F2)-orbit O corresponds to one coarse connected component of degree |O|. The branch permutations are γ0(x,y,z)=(xy−z,x,x²y−xz−y), γ1728(x,y,z)=(y,x,xy−z), γ∞(x,y,z)=(x,z,xz−y); γ−I is the identity. Fibres above 0,1728,∞ are the cycles of the respective permutations, with ramification index equal to cycle length.

**Rotation fibres and their linear operator.** For a,t∈F_q with t≠2, let C_1(a)_t be the x=a fibre of the imported surface X_t(q): y²+z²−ayz+(a²−2−t)=0. Write C_1(a)_t*=C_1(a)_t∩X_t*. The imported cusp rotation acts on (y,z) by L_a=[[0,1],[−1,a]], with characteristic polynomial X²−aX+1. Every point in C_1(a)_t* has (y,z)≠(0,0). Split and nonsplit mean splitting of this polynomial, including in characteristic 2; a discriminant square test is used only when 2 is invertible.

**The exact cusp rotation order.** For q≥3,t≠2 and P=(a,y,z)∈C_1(a)_t*, the orbit of P under γ∞ has length n_q(a). The corresponding γ∞-orbit of an absolutely irreducible non-dihedral representation, modulo diagonal outer action and conjugacy, has the order of its first matrix. Split distinct-root slices reduce to a diagonal matrix with inverse eigenvalues; nonsplit slices use a norm-one eigenvalue in F_{q²}; repeated-root slices have order p or 2p. The condition (y,z)≠(0,0) and the conic equation remove possible shorter eigenline orbits in the exceptional slices.

**SL2 vertical automorphisms.** For q≥3 and absolutely irreducible non-dihedral image G≤SL2(F_q), G contains Z(SL2(F_q)), all geometric vertical automorphism groups of A_G in characteristic zero equal that center, and the rigidified compactified forgetful map Mbar(G)→Ell_1 is representable. On the reduced ramification divisor of a Higman-c stratum the vertical group is Z(SL2(F_q))∩⟨c⟩. It is trivial for even q; for odd q it has order 2 exactly when n_q(tr c) is even, including the noncentral trace −2 case of order 2p.

**SL2 cotangent character exponents.** For q≥3 and G as in the preceding theorem, m_X divides 24 for every component with t≠2. It divides 12 if q is even, or if q is odd and n_q(t) is odd. These bounds use the full stabilizer exponent; m′_X is 1 or 2 as determined by the vertical ramification group, and it is not itself generally 12 or 24.

**SL2 centralizer and cover degrees.** Let q=p^f≥3 and let c∈SL2(F_q) be noncentral with t=tr(c)≠2 and n=|c|. If q is odd and t=−2, then n=2p and |C(c)|=2q, so d_X divides p^(f−1). If X²−tX+1 has distinct roots in F_q, its centralizer is cyclic of order q−1 and d_X divides (q−1)/n. If that polynomial is irreducible over F_q, its centralizer is cyclic of order q+1 and d_X divides (q+1)/n. The last two cases both occur in even characteristic. For a subgroup G as above, C_G(c) embeds in the ambient centralizer and the same divisibility bounds hold.

**SL2 component congruences.** For q=p^f≥3, a nonempty component of A_G,t with t≠2 and absolutely irreducible non-dihedral G≤SL2(F_q) has the following coarse degree divisibility, where n=n_q(t). For q=p odd and t=−2, p divides its degree. For a distinct-root split trace, n/gcd(n,ε(q−1)/n) divides its degree; for an irreducible characteristic polynomial replace q−1 by q+1. Here ε=2 for odd q and ε=1 for even q. Every quotient inside gcd is an integer. The corrected even-q assertion includes nonsplit tori.

**Trace orbit congruences.** For q≥3 and t≠2, put n=n_q(t). In a semisimple case t≠±2, let m=q−1 if X²−tX+1 splits and m=q+1 if it is irreducible. Every Aut^+(F2)-orbit O on X_t*(q) has size divisible by n/gcd(n,4m/n) for odd q and by n/gcd(n,m/n) for even q. These are the moduli after the possible factor-two loss from the component congruence when quotienting by D(q,G). For prime p≥3 and t=−2, every such orbit has size divisible by p. Consequently every orbit of the larger full Markoff move group on the punctured prime-field Markoff surface also has size divisible by p. More generally for t≠±2 and odd ℓ with r=ν_ℓ(n_q(t)),r+s=ν_ℓ(q³−q), every such orbit has size divisible by ℓ^max(r−s,0).

**The split and nonsplit conic fibres.** Let q be odd and t≠2. At a=±2, the full conic C_1(a)_t is empty if t−2 is nonsquare and otherwise is two parallel lines, with 2q points. For distinct split roots of X²−aX+1 it has q−1 points if a²≠t+2, and 2q−1 points, two intersecting lines, if a²=t+2. For irreducible X²−aX+1 it has q+1 points if a²≠t+2, and exactly the single point (a,0,0) if a²=t+2. For even q and t≠0, C_1(0)_t has q points and its rotation orbits have size 2. These statements concern the full conic; X_t* additionally removes every point with fewer than two nonzero coordinates.

stages.title: Markoff modular geometry
stages.description:
**Markoff components and Higman classes.** Let p≥5 be prime. Assume the group generated by Vieta moves and coordinate permutations, without adjoining even sign changes, is transitive on the punctured coefficient-one Markoff surface over F_p (input G-DYNAMICS). Then Aut^+(F2) is already transitive: an orientation-reversing coordinate transposition fixes the point (3,3,3), so the stabilizer meets both orientation cosets. The stack M(SL2(F_p))_{−2} has precisely two geometric connected components, distinguished by the two noncentral trace −2 Higman classes; the diagonal outer involution exchanges them. Each coarse component is isomorphic to the coarse absolute-level curve M_p and has j-degree D=p(p+3) for p≡1 mod4 and p(p−3) for p≡3 mod4. Its compactification is a smooth proper geometrically connected curve.

**Markoff branch and cusp counts.** Under the preceding transitivity hypothesis, put D=p(p+3) or p(p−3) as above. The fibre of the compactified M_p over 0 has (D+2)/3 points: exactly one fixed trace triple (3,3,6) and all other γ0-cycles have length 3. The fibre over 1728 has (D+f_p)/2 points, where f_p=2 for p≡1,7 mod8 and f_p=0 for p≡3,5 mod8. The cusp count is the supplied rotation-orbit count C_p=(p−1)Φ(p−1)/2+(p+1)Φ(p+1)/2+κ_p, with κ_p=(−5p+11)/4 if p≡1 mod4 and (−7p−1)/4 otherwise, and Φ(n)=Σ_{d|n}φ(d)/d. The definition of Φ and the finite-field point/rotation counts belong to ArithmeticDynamicsPartII (routed items 85–86), not a second theory here.

**The genus formula.** Assume p≥5 prime satisfies the transitivity input. Then the common genus of the two compactified trace −2 components equals p²/12−(p−1)Φ(p−1)/4−(p+1)Φ(p+1)/4+ε_p, with ε_p respectively 7p/8−29/24,5p/8+19/24,7p/8−17/24,5p/8+7/24 when p≡1,3,5,7 mod8. It is 0,0,1 for p=5,7,11 and is at least 2 for every p≥13 satisfying the hypothesis. The latter bound uses the explicit lower estimate p²/12−(p−1)^(3/2)/2−(p+1)^(3/2)/2+p/2 and a certified finite check for the remaining primes.

**Finiteness of elliptic j-invariants.** Let K be a number field and p≥13 a prime satisfying the transitivity hypothesis and the verified genus≥2 bound. There are only finitely many geometric elliptic-curve isomorphism classes, equivalently j-invariants in K, admitting a K-rational point on either trace −2 level component; in particular this holds for elliptic curves over K carrying a geometrically connected SL2(F_p)-torsor on E\O with that trace invariant. Apply Faltings after a finite extension over which the geometric components are defined. Do not conclude finiteness of K-isomorphism classes of elliptic curves: quadratic twists preserve j and can produce infinitely many such classes.

**The projective absolute-level quotient.** For p≥5, central twists by Hom(F2,{±I}) give the Klein four action (x,y,z)↦(ε1 x,ε2 y,ε1ε2 z) on X*(p). This is the even sign-change action already owned by CA.4. It is free on the punctured t=−2 locus: a nontrivial fixed sign change forces two zero coordinates and then the third to be zero. The resulting quotient is the finite trace fibre for absolute PSL2(F_p)-structures. Under transitivity its associated coarse component has degree d_p=D/4 and is the curve N_p used for the monodromy statement.

**Large projective monodromy.** Let P_MP be the density-one set of primes p≥5 specified by Meiri–Puder and Chen: p is outside the finite exceptional set E_bgs, and either p≡1 mod4 or p≡3 mod4 with the order of (3+sqrt(5))/2 in F_{p²}^× at least 32sqrt(p+1), interpreted after choosing a root in F_{p²}. For p∈P_MP the geometric monodromy of N_p→P¹_j is S_{d_p} when p≡5,7,9,11 mod16 and A_{d_p} when p≡1,3,13,15 mod16. Its proof requires the independent large-alternating permutation theorem and density result from ArithmeticDynamicsPartII, recorded in G-DYNAMICS, together with the orbit congruence supplied here. The residue classification is a parity computation for the projective branch permutations.

**Noncongruence of Markoff levels.** For p∈P_MP, the finite-index subgroup of SL2(Z) associated to either trace −2 SL2(F_p) component is noncongruence: it contains no principal congruence subgroup. The same obstruction is visible already on the projective absolute quotient N_p, whose monodromy has A_{d_p} as a composition factor with d_p≥7. The only nonabelian simple composition factors of any congruence quotient SL2(Z/n) are PSL2(F_ℓ), and none is isomorphic to A_{d_p} for these d_p≥7. The congruence-subgroup predicate and principal subgroups already exist in Mathlib and are imported unchanged. The composition-factor extension of the existing modular-level quotient theory is requested in Q-CONGRUENCE.
